messages:
jess: Heads-up — a small set of APAC customers saw requests route to eu-west during a short ap-southeast outage, which spiked p95 by ~240ms. They expected ap-southeast fallback to ap-northeast not eu-west. wondering if our region preference / ejection logic mis-ranked regions when probes flapped.

arjun: saw the metric. probes for ap-northeast were noisy during the same window (high probe latency), so the region probe score dropped. fallback picks highest-scoring available region — but we might be overweighting recent probe samples.

maya: are we using simple exponential decay on probe samples? we added faster decay for edge tiers but maybe it's too aggressive. also, how are model-variant fallbacks interacting? some requests hit smaller quantized variant in eu-west which increased token time.

sam_ops: customers on premium plan should probably get stronger affinity to preferred region and model variants. free/standard could be more cost-aware. we currently do per-tenant routing_weights but it's not surfaced in console well.

jess: Agree on surfacing. The UX problem: ops can't tell if a tenant is getting eu-west because of weight vs ejection. Console should show last-region-change reason (probe-eject / quota / manual).

console-ui: noted. we can add a column in per-tenant traces: last_routing_decision and reason, plus a mini timeline. low impact to add as opt-in telemetry.

arjun: proposal: change probe scoring to use two buckets — short-window (15s) for hot failures + long-window (5m) for stability. ejection if short-window error_rate > 5% for 3 probes OR long-window p95 > 300ms. this prevents short spikes from permanently demoting a region.

maya: +1. also add hysteresis for variant swap: if we fallback from base model to quantized variant, do a graceful swap — mark existing KV-cache-enabled connections to drain for N seconds before redirecting new requests. avoids cache-thrashing.

jess: sketch of routing config I'm imagining: 
```json
{
  "routing": {
    "region_preference": ["ap-southeast-1","ap-northeast-1","eu-west-1"],
    "probe_short_ttl_s": 15,
    "probe_long_ttl_s": 300,
    "ejection_threshold": 3,
    "ejection_criteria": {"short_err_pct": 5, "long_p95_ms": 300},
    "variant_fallback": {"graceful": true, "drain_seconds": 30, "max_concurrent_drains": 50}
  }
}
```

sam_ops: love the graceful drain idea. but need a quota/throughput safety net — if draining plus retaining preference exceeds capacity in remaining regions we should allow immediate hard-fallback for high-priority customers. maybe a dual-path fallback: graceful for normal, hard for critical SLA customers.

arjun: agree — add a route_priority field per-tenant: {premium: "hard-first", standard: "graceful-first"}. and a capacity-check before starting drains: if available_capacity < request_rate*1.2 then skip drain.

maya: telemetry changes: add per-tenant region_choice history, variant_used, connection_drain_events, plus per-model latency_kv_hit_rate. we need these to surface regressions after fallback.

jess: on rollout UX — when we flip variant fallback policy we should show an estimated impact calc: how many connections will be drained, estimated extra latency for those clients, and cost delta. console could show a predicted p95 delta using historical traces.

console-ui: we can prototype a rollout modal: selects tenancy scope (all/prefix/tenant), preview impact, run dry-run to collect metrics for one hour, then commit. includes rollback button.

sam_ops: ops-bot note: deployed probe-window change to staging. running 60m canary against a subset of tenants. Will post results. :robot_face:

ops-bot: [deploy] routing/probe-window v0.3 deployed to staging at 1729991290. Canary group: tenant-prefix "apac-canary".

arjun: next steps: instrument the ejection-reason in the router logs (probe_short, probe_long, manual, quota). then wire to console timeline. after canary clear we'll iterate on thresholds.

maya: also add a small tweak: when fallback switches model variant, preserve KV-cache namespace mapping where possible for compatible variants to reduce cold-cache cost.

jess: thanks — this addresses the customer incident root cause and gives us a plan for better visibility. followups: 1) implement two-window probe scoring (arjun) 2) variant graceful drain + cache-preserve (maya) 3) console telemetry + rollout preview (console-ui) 4) ops canary + capacity-safety check (sam_ops).

sam_ops: i'll schedule the canary from 9:30 UTC tomorrow. will ping list with runbook. :calendar:
